preferences.why: Transcript B correctly respects the committed state of Mara standing, whereas Transcript A incorrectly places her sitting on the floor.

Transcript A integrates the committed state of the jumper naturally into the action of the first exchange, has more realistic dialogue about the drying coat, and uses more accurate terminology for a rope splice in the final exchange.
Transcript A has much stronger atmospheric details and character beats, particularly the realistic way she yields to the physical touch and the evocative description of her creased linen shirt.
Transcript B is preferred because its dialogue in the second exchange is much more natural, whereas Transcript A has the character awkwardly narrate her own physical state.
Transcript A is preferred because Transcript B contradicts the player's action in the first exchange by having Mara take and turn the stopcock herself.
Transcript A respects the committed state of Mara standing throughout, whereas Transcript B has her sit down in exchange 2 and remain seated/leaning in exchange 3.
Transcript B is faithful to the committed state of Mara being turned away from Sam, whereas Transcript A has her turn her head to look at him in the first exchange.
Transcript B better respects the tension of the premise; having Mara refuse the tea because her hand is full feels much more realistic than Transcript A, where she casually drinks it anyway.
Transcript B is much more evocative and atmospheric, and it correctly keeps Mara turned away in the second exchange, whereas A violates the state constraint by having her turn her head.
Transcript A uses concrete physical actions, like the thumb pressing the collar of the jumper, to convey subtext and character history while perfectly respecting the covered state of her body.
